Lyle Bongé visited Rondy Rondthaler.
Ben Shahn's lecture at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, in which he praises Black Mountain College (he taught there the previous summer); Rumaker hears him with a friend
Olson draws Rumaker to Black Mountain (an “artful and seductive sales pitch,” the college being in need of students)
First trip to Black Mountain by car (600 miles) with Roger, Marge, and Mary Ann Fretz; arrival at night near the college sign
Rumaker leaves by train for Black Mountain (change at Union Station, Washington: first encounter with the segregated cars of the Southern Railway)

Enrollment of 35 students; Olson on leave, his writing class suspended. Rumaker takes Wes Huss's theater workshop (in the evening, in the dining hall, after dinner), metaphysical poetry with Hilda Morley (in the afternoon, in the library), Natasha Goldowski's modern physics (in the morning, in the lobby of her Meadows Inn apartment), and a French tutorial with Madame Goldowski (in the morning, at Streamside)
Rumaker works in the kitchen; forest fire on the slopes of the Seven Sisters, across from the college: forest rangers come in the evening looking for volunteers
Filling the farm silo: Rumaker, at the top, seized with vertigo
Arrival of Ellen Georgia Schasberger (New York), a new student
Nell Rice receives two or three new students on Sunday evening in her attic apartment in Black Dwarf (supper of cheese and Malrey's bread)
Visit by Glenn, a former student (from Paul Goodman's time), a mathematician at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton
Auditions and first rehearsals of Lorca's Blood Wedding by Wes Huss in the Roadside lobby; Rumaker cast as the Bridegroom
Merrill Gillespie, a music student, in early fall; a student arrives a month after the start of the year to resume his studies with Stefan Wolpe
Wes Huss's anger at Mark Hedden after a skit about Barbara Fritchie, performed after dinner
At dinner, Bach played on recorders in the dining hall, in the early winter dark
Olson's three-week seminar, “Institute of the New Sciences of Man,” with Marie-Louise von Franz, come from Zurich; Rumaker sees her arrive in the kitchen
Olson returns in early spring; first sessions of his class in the afternoon in the meeting room of the office cottage, the warmest
With the good weather, Olson's writing class outdoors, on the terrace of the science building at the top of the hill
Malrey Few invites Mary Fiore and Rumaker to her nephew Alvin's 8th-grade graduation in Asheville, one Sunday afternoon
Summer Institute of the Arts: Esteban Vicente's drawing class under the Studies Building, in the open air, with nude models (including Hilda Morley)
So many guests during a summer institute that Rumaker sets up extra tables from the porch to the Round House veranda
John Cage at the college: Rumaker, sweeping the dining hall, at first takes him for a workman
James Leo Herlihy and Remy Charlip come back for the summer institute and join Merce Cunningham's dance class
A German pianist plays Boulez's Second Sonata (premiered at the college by David Tudor in summer 1951); Olson corresponds with Boulez to invite him
Timber cutting on the property to keep the college going in 1953 and beyond: log trucks all day on the college road
Logging crews with Olson (chain saw): there is money for coal only for the Studies Building
The first copies of the Maximus Poems 1-10, published by Jonathan Williams (Jargon), arrive from Stuttgart
Departure of Johanna Jalowetz
Natasha Goldowski leaves the college with Eric Renner and her mother for a small rented farm near Beaucatcher Mountain
One of the last parties in the dining hall before the lower campus is closed
Winter work break: Rumaker in New York, in the Village (apartment shared with Mary Ann Fretz)
Rumaker returns for the spring quarter; moves into the ground floor of Meadows Inn (Natasha and Eric's former apartment) with Tom Field and Terence Burns
Arrival of Robert Creeley, who left Majorca on March 13, expected at the end of March to teach, with the copies of the first issue of the Black Mountain Review
Creeley's first writing class: Rumaker reads excerpts from his diary
Betty Kaiser abruptly leaves the college for New York (in fact to have Olson's child)
After the spring quarter, Rumaker and Tom Field hitchhike to New Orleans (about five days)
Doyle Jones leaves the farm
Departure of Flola Shepard; Robert Hellman, the new writing teacher, moves into her quarters
Arrival of Betty Baker (former editor of the North Carolina Historical Review) as administrative secretary
Rumaker's correspondence with Creeley, back in Majorca, begins
The faculty decides to close the college for the winter to save coal; the students are said to be “at work in the field”
Rumaker returns to the college, end of February 1955
Loan of 287.50 dollars for tuition, so that he can graduate
Olson points out a short story contest for North Carolina students (Greensboro College arts festival); “The Pipe” is sent in
Arrival of John Wieners and his friend Dana, who drove down from Boston
Saturday evening party in the lobby of Streamside, where Wieners lives, organized by Wieners and Rumaker
Graduation project set by Olson: at least six essays on Shakespeare's plays (Lear, Macbeth, Coriolanus, Timon, Pericles, Hamlet, Othello, Richard II, The Tempest, The Winter's Tale)
Creeley returns from Majorca; the college's situation has deteriorated
Birth of Charles Peter, son of Olson and Betty Kaiser
Rumaker graduates, with Jorge Fick and Ed Dorn: “a 1955 class of three, the last graduates of the school”; an outside examiner for each (Franz Kline for Fick), oral before the whole faculty
Olson, the last to leave, completes the liquidation of the college
